author: reek
body: Two chapters in one compilation unit each define collide-helper, with the same type and different answers. This is legal and it compiles, and that is the whole problem: ChapterScoper mangles both, each chapter keeps its own, and nothing in either file says the name is contested.

author: reek
body: The warning under test is CDX3006, raised once at each definition site. It is a warning and not an error because a collision is sometimes deliberate, so this test must COMPILE and RUN, not fail.

author: reek
body: The runtime answer is the second half of the claim. CollideBeta's opening calls collide-helper without qualification and gets BETA's definition, because a mention resolves in the chapter it sits in. Move that same line into CollideAlpha and it would answer 2 instead of 101, with no diagnostic and no textual difference.
